title: fix: move code agent sync into the repository row
author: ElliotEtag
pr_body_excerpt:
The edit dialog for code agents had "Sync from GitHub" alone in its own panel, away from the repository it acts on, and the repository label drifted below its input because it was centred against the "Fork an example" link too.

- Moves Sync next to the locked repository input; while editing, the line under it shows the deployed commit (`Synced to <sha>` after a sync) instead of the fork link
- Sync is an outlined button and shows a spinner instead of swapping its label, since it redeploys immediately rather than on Save
- The sync handler returns the new commit from the existing sync response
- Adds a `note` slot to `ModelFormRow` so lines under a control no longer pull the label off-centre; "Fork an example" now sits left-aligned under the input at its own width

gist.headline: Sync found its repository
gist.blurb: The Sync button moves in beside the repository it actually syncs. A little commit SHA under the input confirms where the code agent landed.
gist.summary: The code-agent edit dialog moves Sync from its own panel beside the locked repository input, shows the deployed commit as “Synced to <sha>” after an immediate redeploy, and adds a ModelFormRow note slot to keep labels aligned.
gist.impact: People editing code agents get the sync action and deployed commit together, with a spinner during sync and no need to press Save to redeploy.
gist.visual_concept: A cozy code-garden workbench represents the code-agent edit dialog: a repository input and Sync button sit side by side, with a short commit SHA beneath them. Polli, wearing a tiny tool belt, points to the commit marker; neatly aligned labels and a code-plant reinforce the tidier layout.
